Description: Confirm the deployed ADA REST and SSE operations required by the pilot.
Acceptance criteria: Session creation, prompt submission, streaming, history access and correlation fields are recorded. WebSockets and direct runner integration are excluded.

Description: Verify that the deployed ADA configuration persists Session conversation, events and state in the environment PostgreSQL service.
Acceptance criteria: A Session survives instance replacement and can be continued through a healthy instance. MOSAIC does not recreate ADA persistence.

Story: Pin the current catalogue and snapshot
Description: Use reviewed Git content for the Public Skill catalogue and current JSON capability snapshot for Release 1.
Acceptance criteria: A deployment uses an explicit Git revision. Every replica loads the same Skill and JSON content at startup. No database-backed Integration publication is introduced.

Description: Run a representative read-only OpenShift investigation through ADA and the existing MOSAIC orchestrator.
Acceptance criteria: A prompt reaches MOSAIC, invokes only approved read-only tools and streams a useful response to a minimal client. Session and request IDs are retained.

Description: Capture only the confirmed interfaces that the access API and web application must use.
Acceptance criteria: Request, response, SSE, Session and error contracts are versioned. Unknowns become targeted stories rather than broad discovery work.

Description: Define the minimal external API for authentication, Sessions, prompts, streaming and Public Skill selection.
Acceptance criteria: The API delegates orchestration to ADA and MOSAIC. It does not implement Goals, tool routing, Integration authoring or a general gateway platform.

Description: Resolve a high-entropy development token to one Human Account.
Acceptance criteria: Only a salted token hash is stored. Tokens can expire and be revoked. Caller-supplied identity headers are ignored. The mode cannot start outside development.

Description: Provide controlled CLI or SQL tooling for Human Account and token administration.
Acceptance criteria: No administration UI is added. Plaintext tokens are shown once. Revocation blocks subsequent requests.

Description: Create opaque ADA Sessions and verify Account ownership on every Session operation.
Acceptance criteria: Session IDs are generated at a trusted boundary. An Account cannot list, read, resume or invoke another Account's Session.

Description: Send an authenticated prompt to ADA and stream the response through the access API.
Acceptance criteria: The same correlation identifiers are preserved. Sensitive headers and tokens never appear in URLs or streamed content. A dropped client does not duplicate the request.

Story: Support direct Human Account API use
Description: Allow an invited Human Account to call the same API without using the web application.
Acceptance criteria: Bearer-token authentication and Session ownership are identical for web and direct API use. Service identities and unattended automation are excluded.

Story: Enforce one active request per Session
Description: Prevent concurrent requests from mutating the same Session while allowing different Sessions to run concurrently.
Acceptance criteria: Conflicts return HTTP 409 with the Session identifier and an exact reason. Requests are not silently queued.

Description: Map authentication, ownership, conflict, ADA and provider failures into stable API responses.
Acceptance criteria: Responses contain an actionable message and correlation ID without prompts, tool arguments, Evidence, tokens or backend inventories.

Story: Create the minimal web application shell
Description: Create an independently deployable web application containing only authentication, Sessions, Public Skills and chat navigation.
Acceptance criteria: There are no administration, Integration authoring, publication or chargeback pages.

Story: Use a development token in the web application
Description: Allow an invited user to provide or receive a development token for the current pilot.
Acceptance criteria: The token is sent only in the Authorization header and is not written to URLs, analytics or browser logs. Invalid and expired tokens are handled explicitly.

Story: Submit a prompt and render the streamed response
Description: Connect the chat view to the access API using REST and SSE.
Acceptance criteria: The user sees streaming progress and the final response. Reconnection does not create a second request. Correlation information is available for support.

Description: Provide the minimum Session navigation needed to start and continue conversations.
Acceptance criteria: Only owned Sessions are shown. Selecting a completed Session preserves conversation history and the next prompt starts a new Goal.

Description: Show request-in-progress, clarification, completion, conflict and failure states.
Acceptance criteria: The composer cannot create concurrent work in one Session. Messages state what happened and what the user can do next without vague retry wording.

Description: Render an orchestrator clarification as part of the conversation and let the user answer it in the same Session.
Acceptance criteria: The answer continues the existing Goal using the current orchestrator behaviour. Changing topic or abandoning a clarification is explicitly outside Release 1.

Story: Create the minimal MOSAIC database boundary
Description: Create MOSAIC-owned tables within the environment's single PostgreSQL service.
Acceptance criteria: MOSAIC and ADA use separate roles and tables. Migrations are repeatable. Tables are limited to Accounts, token metadata, Session ownership and enabled Skill mappings.

Story: Persist Human Accounts and Session ownership
Description: Persist the minimum trusted ownership model used by the access API.
Acceptance criteria: Each Session has exactly one Human Account owner. No workspace, team, tenant administration or Service identity model is implemented.

Description: Read safe discovery metadata from the validated Git Skill catalogue.
Acceptance criteria: Name, description, version, domain and function are visible. Provider endpoints, credentials and Integration internals are excluded.

Description: Let users discover Skills by hierarchy, name and description.
Acceptance criteria: All Public Skills remain visible whether enabled or not. The hierarchy supports domain and function browsing.

Description: Store one personal set of enabled Public Skill names per Human Account.
Acceptance criteria: New Accounts start empty. Unknown or duplicate Skill names are rejected. Skill content remains in Git.

Description: Allow a user to change its own enabled Public Skill set.
Acceptance criteria: Operations are Account-owned and idempotent. The UI confirms the resulting set. Changes do not affect active work.

Description: Enable all Skills currently published in a selected domain or function.
Acceptance criteria: The UI previews the exact Skill names and count. Explicit Skill names are stored. Later additions are not enabled automatically.

Story: Resolve enabled Skills at a new Goal
Description: Use the Account's current enabled Skill set when MOSAIC starts a new Goal.
Acceptance criteria: The loaded set is fixed for that Goal. An in-flight or clarification-held Goal is unchanged. The next Goal sees subsequent Skill changes.

Description: Exercise Sessions, history and enabled Skills using at least two synthetic Human Accounts.
Acceptance criteria: Neither Account can list, read, resume, invoke or change the other's state. Logs, caches and errors do not expose cross-Account data.

Description: Prevent the temporary bearer-token mode from starting outside the development environment.
Acceptance criteria: Startup fails closed outside development. Logs identify the configured auth mode without exposing token material.

Description: Confirm every Release 1 MCP server and permitted tool runs in read-only mode.
Acceptance criteria: The runtime allowlist contains only required read operations. Mutation attempts fail. Shared provider identity is documented as a development limitation.

Description: Expose basic health and preserve Account, Session, Goal and request correlation through supported components.
Acceptance criteria: Health distinguishes startup/configuration failure from dependency failure. Logs omit tokens, prompts, arguments and Evidence.

Description: Test invalid authentication, Session conflict, dropped SSE, ADA failure, MCP failure and invalid startup configuration.
Acceptance criteria: Failures produce stable responses, do not leak sensitive detail and never create duplicate requests or cross-Account state.

Story: Run the complete two-Account pilot regression
Description: Run the web and direct API paths with two Accounts using different enabled Skills.
Acceptance criteria: Authentication, Session continuation, Skill selection, read-only investigation and isolation pass through the deployed environment.

Description: Provide the deployment, user-provisioning, configuration and support information required for the controlled pilot.
Acceptance criteria: The documentation states development-only authentication, shared provider identity, read-only scope, current Git/JSON configuration and all deferred production capabilities.

Description: Demonstrate the agreed Release 1 outcome using the deployed development environment.
Acceptance criteria: Two provisioned users choose different Public Skills, run useful investigations, continue their own Sessions and cannot access each other's state. Deferred work is not required to pass.

Description: Replace development tokens with authorization code and PKCE using validated issuer and subject claims.
Acceptance criteria: OIDC is required before production access.

Description: Support non-human access without impersonating Human Accounts.
Acceptance criteria: Service identities own independent Sessions, Skills, quotas and audit identity.

Description: Add idempotency and lifecycle behaviour for unattended API calls.
Acceptance criteria: Retries cannot create duplicate Goals and automation cannot access Human Sessions.

Story: Define the reusable MCP shim contract
Description: Specify trusted identity, forwarding, audit and error behaviour for vendor MCP servers.
Acceptance criteria: The contract cannot trust caller-supplied identity headers.

Description: Validate short-lived credentials and reject spoofed identity.
Acceptance criteria: Issuer, audience, signature and expiry are enforced consistently.

Description: Translate trusted identity into the access mechanisms supported by OpenShift, Oracle, MQ and later providers.
Acceptance criteria: Each provider remains the authoritative data and action access-control point.

Description: Create normalized, versioned tables for Targets, Providers, Capabilities, bindings, Routing, extraction and limits.
Acceptance criteria: A publication is immutable and identified by snapshot_id.

Story: Import and publish reviewed Integration data
Description: Validate existing JSON and publish its normalized representation transactionally.
Acceptance criteria: The JSON document itself is not stored in PostgreSQL.

Description: Reconstruct the runtime snapshot from normalized rows at startup.
Acceptance criteria: Every runtime replica in a deployment uses the same explicit snapshot_id.

Story: Store complete Skill versions in PostgreSQL
Description: Move Skill content, ownership, visibility and lifecycle from Git to the strategic catalogue.
Acceptance criteria: Published Skill versions are immutable.

Description: Allow user-authored Skills to reference only approved read-only Capabilities.
Acceptance criteria: Users cannot introduce Providers, Targets, endpoints or bindings.

Description: Require independent review before any Public Skill version is published.
Acceptance criteria: Authors cannot approve their own Public versions.

Description: Publish reusable Skills to selected organisational groups without introducing shared workspaces.
Acceptance criteria: Group membership controls discovery, not underlying provider RBAC.

Description: Deploy authoring independently from the runtime web application and request path.
Acceptance criteria: Workbench failure cannot affect runtime traffic.

Description: Show Skill to Capability to binding to Provider to Target relationships.
Acceptance criteria: Missing and conflicting links are visible.

Description: Validate schema, references, Routing, extraction and limits before publication.
Acceptance criteria: Invalid drafts cannot become active and previous publications remain available for rollback.

Story: Add explicit stop and Goal cancellation
Description: Cancel an active Goal terminally and prevent late results from changing state.
Acceptance criteria: Cancelled Goals are never resumed.

Story: Support abandoning clarification for a new topic
Description: Let a user terminate a clarification-held Goal and start another Goal explicitly.
Acceptance criteria: The model is not the sole transition authority.

Description: MOSAIC owner
Acceptance criteria: Expiry remains configurable and can be disabled.

Description: MOSAIC owner
Acceptance criteria: 429 responses state the exact limit and retry condition or reset time.

Story: Assess ADA and GCP usage granularity
Description: Verify whether model and runtime usage can be attributed to Account, Session, Goal and request.
Acceptance criteria: An evidence-backed gap report precedes any new ledger.

Story: Add a minimal usage ledger only if required
Description: Track only the usage and cost fields missing from existing telemetry.
Acceptance criteria: The ledger excludes prompts, responses, arguments and Evidence.
